study type: Retrospective observational study, interrupted time series analysis
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic (pre-pandemic, during first year of pandemic, after vaccination)
outcome: Monthly utilization rates of neuraxial anaesthesia (NA)
Caesarean section urgency (Category-1 caesarean section events)
Composite adverse neonatal outcomes (stillbirths, Apgar 5-min score < 7)
cohort: The study included 9,744 consecutive women (7,083 Turkish citizens and 2,661 migrants) who underwent singleton caesarean sections between March 2018 and March 2023 at a single tertiary care hospital in Istanbul.
finding: During the COVID-19 pandemic, there was a continuation of the upward trend in the use of neuraxial anaesthesia for caesarean sections, with an immediate significant increase at the pandemic's onset for both Turkish citizens and migrants.
mod_finding: The choice of anaesthetic technique for caesarean sections showed an increasing trend in the use of neuraxial anaesthesia throughout the study period, with an immediate significant increase at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
